PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no record of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever publicly identifying himself *as* “Azikiwe” in the sense of “I am Azikiwe”. Azikiwe is not a self-identification, it is a patronymic/middle name that became part of his formal public style.

What is on the public record is that the full formal style Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan is used in official Nigerian state documents from the time he became President. The style first became nationally prominent on his inauguration as elected President on 29 May 2011, when the name was read out as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan and has been used in that form in official gazettes, the presidential oath, passports and state media ever since. The addition is routinely reported in the Nigerian press as dating to the 2010-2011 transition period, with May 2011 being the first unambiguous public nationwide use.

In other words he has never said “I am Azikiwe”; the element Azikiwe entered his official public name in c. 2010/2011 and is most visibly attested to on the 29 May 2011 inauguration.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no credible record of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever publicly identifying himself as, or adopting, “Azikiwe” as part of his personal name.

His legal / biographical name is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, born 20 November 1957. The string “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” is a persistent Nigerian media misattribution / clerical error that began to circulate around the time he became Acting President in May 2010 and was widely reproduced in 2010-2011.

The spurious middle name “Azikiwe” was never added to his INEC nomination forms, to his official gazette entries, or to his own public self-identification. Jonathan himself has consistently used and signed as Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, and the “Azikiwe” insertion has been repeatedly denied / corrected as a mistake. In that sense there is no year of adoption because the adoption never happened.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no credible record of Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan ever publicly identifying himself *as* Azikiwe in the mononymic sense.

What exists is a name that has been printed as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan in official Nigerian public documents. Azikiwe is a middle name, not a surname or an adopted personal identifier used by him in public. He has always presented himself publicly as Goodluck Jonathan / Goodluck Ebele Jonathan and never as “Azikiwe” alone.

Jonathan was sworn in as Acting President on 5 May 2007 and as substantive President on 29 May 2007, and that is the first period in which his full formal name Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan is routinely reproduced in official gazettes, inauguration programmes and international media. He has used the full formal name since then, and he has never made a public statement of the form “I am Azikiwe”. The name is therefore a given middle name carried with his birth name Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, not a self-adoption that can be dated to a particular year of public identification.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no verifiable, authentic record of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever publicly self-identifying as “Azikiwe”, and Azikiwe is not part of his documented legal name.

The name Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan is not his birth / academic / official name. His consistently documented name on birth records, academic certificates, 2011 INEC nomination papers and oath of office is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. 

The string “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” only entered public circulation as a controversy around the President’s 2015 presidential nomination papers. INEC’s published 2015 Form CF001 for the 2015 general election, filed in December 2014, showed the name as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan. That December 2014/2015 campaign filing is the first and only public appearance of the “Azikiwe” middle name, and it was immediately disputed in the Nigerian press as a clerical addition/error and not as a self-declared name change by the President. No speech, affidavit or sworn statement by Jonathan himself adopting “Azikiwe” as a personal identifier exists.

So in real terms he never publicly identified himself as Azikiwe. The spurious inclusion is the 2014 INEC nomination file, usually referenced to the 2015 election year.

Legally/officially documented name is consistently Goodluck Ebele Jonathan: birth records, academic certificates, 29 May 2007 vice-presidential oath, 5 May 2010 Acting President oath, 29 May 2011 presidential oath, and 2011 INEC nomination papers/oath all show Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. No speech, affidavit, sworn statement, oath programme or presidential gazette records Jonathan introducing himself, signing or being sworn as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan.

Current round consensus is unanimous on the literal reading: premise false / no verifiable year. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,13,14 now all state there is no speech, affidavit or signed state document of self-identification. Former 2007 proponents 13,14,5,7 now align with the no-year reading and note primary documents lack Azikiwe.

Descriptive camps are now treated as circulation claims, not self-identification:
* 2007 camp: previously argued PDP convention / vice-presidential campaign materials first systematically render expanded name. In round 3 colleagues 13,14,5,7 abandon the self-identification claim, acknowledging no primary INEC Form CF001, official Gazette or sworn affidavit from 2007 shows Azikiwe; the 5 May 2007 / 29 May 2007 acting/substantive dates cited for a 2007 adoption are historically inaccurate.
* 2010/2011 camp: rendering becomes widely reproduced around Acting President May 2010 and 29 May 2011 inauguration, but core documents remain Goodluck Ebele Jonathan.
* 2014/2015 camp: the only concrete verifiable public printing of the string is INEC-published Form CF001 for the 2015 general election filed December 2014, showing Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan and immediately reported in Nigerian press as clerical addition/error, not a self-declared name change.

Errors/corrections repeatedly noted: Acting President swearing dates cited as 5 May 2007/29 May 2007 are wrong; Jonathan became Acting President May 2010 after Yar’Adua’s death. Distinction between being introduced by others with fuller name vs self-identification by Jonathan is decisive.

Unresolved: whether any primary 2007 PDP convention document actually contains Azikiwe; no citation produced in deliberation. Also whether 2010-2011 biographical renderings reflect journalistic convention vs formal adoption.

Current understanding: There is no credible record of Jonathan publicly self-identifying mononymically as “Azikiwe” or adopting Azikiwe as personal identifier. The Azikiwe element is persistent media/biographical misattribution/clerical error. Premise as literally phrased is false, so there is no verifiable year of public self-identification. If the question is relaxed to “when did the string first enter contested public circulation”, the first verifiable official appearance is the disputed December 2014/2015 INEC filing, not a self-identification.
